markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (81%)** · Ambiguous: Benign vs InSitu · Careful review
InSitu is in the 90% conformal set; invasive probability is under 1% [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 81%, InSitu 16% | Benign leads clearly |
| Conformal set | Benign, InSitu | Two classes not separable |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.95 / 90th percentile | Input not flagged |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Independent model agrees |
| Similar cases | 2 of 5 Benign | Mixed neighbor labels |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 3) · ↑ invasive · Below typical; concept model leans away from invasion [F3] · Validated (19/20)
- **Tumor cell fraction** (regions 0, 5, 11) · context · 86% neoplastic nuclei, top of reference set; sampled regions [F7] · Measured
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (regions 1, 6, 10) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; fits in situ or benign · Weak (12/20)
- **Frequent mitotic figures** (regions 1, 5, 6) · ↑ invasive · Above typical; failed AI spot check, disregard [F2] · Unreliable (0/20)

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion effect 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0; not shown faithful. This case leans on Unreliable mitoses and normal lobules (both 0/20).

## Could be wrong if
- Region 5 alone scores 47% invasive risk; other regions score near 0.
- Tumor cell fraction is top of the reference range, yet the call is benign.

## Check on the slide
1. **Region 5**: confirm or exclude invasive growth; its per-region risk is 47%.
2. **Regions 1, 6, 10**: separate duct-confined atypia from benign hyperplasia.
3. **Regions 0, 5, 11**: verify the high neoplastic nuclei count is truly tumor.
